notes.gasoline_thesis: MY INFERENCE, not a sourced claim. Gasoline prices ROSE through BJ's Q1 (Jan $2.81 -> May $4.48) and management said fuel 'margins were pressured early in the period as prices moved higher'. They FELL through Q2 ($4.48 -> $3.93), which is normally a fuel-margin-dollar tailwind. Combined with CFO Felice's pre-flagged 'additional tariff dollars that flow into Q2', this is the most credible source of an EPS upside surprise and is probably not precisely modelled by the Street. It does NOT help the ex-gas comp, which is the metric that prices the stock.
notes.triage_rationale_response: The triage note was 'universe at or below the triage threshold - all eligible names carried forward', i.e. BJ was carried by default rather than selected on merit. I disagree with the implied dismissal. This is a live, tradeable event: a 6.75% implied move on a $11.7B name, a bimodal realised-move distribution (1.1-1.5% or 6.8-12.2%), a published pass/fail threshold from management's own mouth, adverse alt-data on that exact threshold, 6.4-7.5% short interest, and a -6.8% run-in. It deserves panel time. What it does NOT deserve is high confidence in a direction.
